comment: The decisive reversal was D<E: the residual ReLU network outperformed the deeper plain SiLU network despite having two fewer layer norms. Preserved input-dependent features and faster rectifier fitting are plausible explanations, not measured mechanisms. I overextended K1074’s normalized-depth preference beyond its shallow-rival scope; K1006 explicitly warns against ordering these bundles by LN count, and K1008 does not settle unequal-LN/topology comparisons. Backtesting found no exact-scope historical or lab comparisons. Broadening to residual rectifiers versus plain smooth networks with more LN yielded one low-rate historical comparison, which favored the smooth network; three higher-rate lab comparisons favored rectifiers, across three sets with other knobs confounded. These results do not support a general D-over-E rule.
